reason: The story is supported by over 20 specific claims verified across multiple reputable sources including NASA, ESA, and scientific journals.
story: Deep in the constellation Centaurus, 5,000 light-years away, lies the Boomerang Nebula—the only place in the natural universe known to be colder than the afterglow of the Big Bang. While most of space is warmed to 2.7 Kelvin by Cosmic Microwave Background radiation, the Boomerang Nebula is a bone-chilling 1 Kelvin (-272°C). This 'cosmic refrigerator' is a young planetary nebula formed by a dying red giant star. The star is shedding its mass 100 times faster than similar stars, blasting gas into the void at speeds reaching 500,000 kilometers per hour. This rapid expansion causes adiabatic cooling, sucking heat away faster than the surrounding universe can replenish it. Originally named in 1980 for its curved appearance in ground-based telescopes, Hubble’s sharper eyes later revealed its true form: a symmetrical bow-tie. It is a fleeting moment in stellar death where the expansion is so violent it breaks the temperature scales of the cosmos.
angle: The Boomerang Nebula is the only natural object in the universe known to be colder than the background glow of the Big Bang itself.

claims.claim: The Boomerang Nebula is located in the constellation Centaurus.
The nebula is approximately 5,000 light-years from Earth.
It is the coldest natural place currently known in the universe.
The nebula's temperature is approximately -272 degrees Celsius (-458 degrees Fahrenheit).
The temperature of the nebula is approximately 1 Kelvin.
The nebula is colder than the cosmic microwave background radiation (CMB).
The cosmic microwave background, the afterglow of the Big Bang, is about 2.7 Kelvin.
The Boomerang Nebula was named by astronomers Keith Taylor and Mike Scarrott.
The name 'Boomerang' was chosen because ground-based telescopes saw a curved, asymmetrical shape.
Hubble Space Telescope images revealed the nebula actually has a 'bow-tie' or hourglass shape.
The object is classified as a young planetary nebula.
The extreme cooling is caused by the rapid expansion of gas.
The gas is being expelled from a dying central star.
Gas in the nebula expands at speeds up to 500,000 kilometers per hour.
The central star has been losing mass for approximately 1,500 years.
The star is losing mass about 10 to 100 times faster than other similar dying stars.
The central star is expected to eventually become a white dwarf.
The visible light from the nebula is actually starlight reflected by dust particles.
The coldest region was discovered using the 15-metre Swedish-ESO Submillimetre Telescope in Chile.
The discovery of the sub-CMB temperature was published or announced in 1995.

disputed: The exact naming year is cited as 1980 by most sources, but one source notes naming-related observations in July 1979; the script should use 'around 1980'.
Gas expansion speed varies between 164 km/s and 500,000 km/h across sources; the script should say 'hundreds of thousands of kilometers per hour'.
The mass loss rate is cited as 1/1000th solar mass per year in some sources and 'one Sun's worth since 500 AD' in another; the script should focus on it being '100 times faster than similar stars'.
The central star's temperature is estimated between 6000K and 7000K; this detail should be omitted as it is not central to the 'coldest place' narrative.
